paper_sections.title: Binge Eating (BE) and Obesity: Brain Activity and Psychological Measures before and after Roux-En-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB)
3.4.3. Change in Activation from Baseline to 4 Months Post (T1 > T2)

description.value: The study examined brain activity and psychological measures related to binge eating and obesity before and four months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, compared with BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment.

design.value: A prospective longitudinal comparison of 15 women with obesity who opted for RYGB surgery and 13 BMI-matched women with obesity who did not undergo treatment, assessed approximately one month before and four months after surgery or a matched interval. Only women were included, and participants were classified as binge eating or non-binge eating according to DSM-5 criteria.

name.value: Questionnaire of Eating and Weight Patterns Revised (QEWP-R)

description.value: Questionnaire used to assess binge eating and eating and weight patterns; it was completed at baseline and used again to reassess binge-eating status at four months.
Questionnaire completed at baseline and used with the QEWP-R in classifying participants according to binge-eating status.
Follow-up questionnaire used at four months to reassess binge-eating status; it included modified questions pertaining to bariatric surgery in place of the EDE-Q.

The EMAQ assesses emotional eating in response to positive and negative emotions and situations. It contains 22 questions, with Likert-scale scores from 1 to 9, and mean scores are calculated for positive and negative emotions and situations.

The PFS assesses the impact of food-abundant environments, including appetite-related thoughts, feelings, and motivations, at three levels of food proximity: food available (Abstract), food present (Presence), and food tasted (Pleasure).
BMI was included as a nuisance covariate in the second-level fMRI multiple regression analyses and as a covariate in the baseline MANCOVA.
Body weight was measured at baseline and four months post-surgery.
Body fat was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis with a Tanita scale.

task_description.value: Participants viewed high energy-density food, low energy-density food, and non-food visual stimuli in the scanner across six runs. Each run consisted of 10 stimuli of the same type, presented for four seconds each, preceded by a 52-second crosshairs baseline and followed by a 40-second crosshairs baseline; each stimulus type was repeated twice with different stimuli.

stimuli.value: HEF stimuli included cakes, ice cream, and fast foods; LEF stimuli consisted of fruits and vegetables; NF stimuli consisted of basic office supplies such as tape, staplers, and rubber bands. HEF stimuli had an energy density of at least 3.5 kcal/g and LEF stimuli had an energy density less than 1 kcal/g.

instrument.value: 1.5 GE Tesla twin-speed scanner with supine quadrature RF head coil

description.value: Functional T2*-weighted images were acquired with a gradient echo pulse sequence. Scans were conducted in the morning between 9–11 am, keeping the same time for a given participant. The visual stimuli were presented through goggles in six runs. Each run lasted two minutes and 12 seconds and included 36 whole-brain scans, each consisting of 25 contiguous slices parallel to the AC/PC line.

Prior to statistical analyses, the realigned T2*-weighted volumes were slice-time corrected, spatially transformed to a standardized Montreal Neurologic Institute brain, and smoothed with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: Spatial transformation to a standardized Montreal Neurologic Institute brain.
Spatial smoothing with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: First-level regressors were created by convolving the onset of each condition with the canonical HRF with duration of 40 s. Contrasts were created for Food > NF and HEF > LEF at T1, T2, and T1 > T2.

model_type.value: group random effects (2nd-level) multiple regression analyses

model_settings.value: Contrasts of parameter estimates from the first-level models were entered into second-level multiple regression analyses with predictor variables for experimental group (BE vs. NB), intervention group (RYGB vs. NT), and BMI as a nuisance covariate. Main comparisons included overall effects at T1, T2, and T1 > T2 and two-way interactions between experimental and intervention groups.

One-way ANOVA was conducted on baseline characteristics, including age, BMI, weight, and body fat percentage, to compare treatment groups and BE versus NB status. One-way ANOVA was also conducted for weight change from baseline to four months between treatment groups.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), 21st and 22nd Editions

model_settings.value: Baseline MANCOVA tested the effect of binge-eating status on two emotional eating measures and three PFS measures, with baseline BMI as a covariate.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), 21st and 22nd Editions

model_settings.value: ANCOVA was conducted for the four-month outcome psychological measures, with the baseline score entered as a covariate. Treatment and binge-eating status were entered as fixed factors.

software.value: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), 21st and 22nd Editions

model_settings.value: Because of outliers, non-normal data, and unequal variances, 1,000 bootstrap samples were performed using a bias-corrected and accelerated confidence interval. Test statistics for the original, unsampled data were reported, while p-values were estimated using nonparametric bootstrapping.
